# Issues and the board: gh dojo

This project tracks the issues of Trum-ok/gh-dojo on the GitHub Projects board of Trum-ok, project 5, with the process in `.github/dojo.toml` (preset `kanban`). Take, move, comment on, block and create issues **only** through `gh dojo`: never change a status, a comment, a blocked-by link or an issue with `gh issue`, `gh project` or the API. For what gh dojo cannot do, such as editing an issue's title, body, labels or assignees, use `gh issue` only when the task needs it or the user asks.

Everything below is enough for everyday work; read `gh dojo <command> --help` only when a command refuses or you need a flag not named here. When the setup is broken (token, board, config), `gh dojo doctor` names each problem with the command that fixes it.

A bare `12` or `#12` is an issue of `Trum-ok/gh-dojo`; an issue of another repository is `owner/repo#12` or its URL.

## Lifecycle

`Backlog` → `In progress` → (`Waiting`) → `Ready` → `Done`, through `start`, `wait`, `ready`, `done`. A status in parentheses may be skipped.

- `Backlog` is the initial status: `gh dojo new` puts new issues there, and an issue without a status or not on the board counts as `Backlog`.
- Final: `Done`. `gh dojo list` hides issues there unless `--all`.
- A blocker is resolved, no longer blocking, when it is closed or in `Ready` or `Done`, though it may be open; one whose status could not be read (`status not read: …`) still blocks.

## Verbs

Run a verb as `gh dojo <verb> N`; `--dry-run` prints its plan without changing anything, and `--show` also prints the issue's card, as `gh dojo show N` does. A verb adds the issue to the board if it is missing and refuses a closed issue unless noted. It confirms in one line, such as `#42 Backlog → In progress, comment left`: there is no need to read the issue again.

`N…` takes several numbers at once: one that fails is skipped and named in the summary.

**`start`** (you take an issue to work on): `gh dojo start N…`, Backlog, Waiting, Ready → In progress; optional --comment; assigns you; comments "Taken. Session: {session} {comment}".

- With an unresolved blocker it warns on stderr and still runs: read the card (`--show`) and decide whether to keep the issue, or ask the user.

**`wait`** (work has stopped: waiting for another issue or an outside decision): `gh dojo wait N…`, In progress → Waiting; needs --by or --comment; comments "Waiting for {by}. {comment}".

- `--by 12` also marks the issue blocked by #12; text (`--by "the user's decision"`) only goes into the comment.

**`ready`** (done, checked and committed to main): `gh dojo ready N…`, In progress, Waiting → Ready; comments only with --comment.

**`done`** (the change has shipped in a release): `gh dojo done N…`, Ready → Done; also on closed issues; comments only with --comment; closes as completed.

- For a release, `gh dojo release <tag> --verb done --dry-run` lists the issues the release includes and its plan; read `gh dojo release --help` before you run it.

**`shipped`** (the issue is for work already shipped in a release): `gh dojo shipped N…`, Backlog → Done; needs --comment; also on closed issues; assigns you; comments "Already shipped: {comment}"; closes as completed.

**`plan`** (the issue moves to another stage): `gh dojo plan N…`, Backlog, In progress, Waiting, Ready → status unchanged; needs --milestone; sets the --milestone milestone.

- `--milestone <title>`, or a start only that title has (`--milestone v1.2`): ask the user which milestone if you do not know. `--milestone none` takes the issue out of its milestone.

## Reading

- `gh dojo next`: what to take next, the open issues in `Backlog` or without a status, with no unresolved blocker, in board order, 5 by default (`--limit N`). The blocked ones are hidden and counted; `--all` shows them with their blockers. Filters: `--mine`, `--label <label>`. Once you pick one, `gh dojo start N --show`: it takes the issue and prints its card.
- `gh dojo show N` before you work on an issue (to take it as well, `gh dojo start N --show` prints the same card): its status, blockers both ways, parent and sub-issues, history, description and the last 5 comments; `--comments all` prints the whole thread, `--full` everything uncut (a verb takes both too). Several numbers print three lines per issue.
- `gh dojo list`: an overview of the board, when the user asks for one: the open issues grouped by status; closed issues and final statuses are hidden and counted; `Ready` is one line of numbers, `--status Ready` lists them with titles. Filters: `--status "<status>"`, `--status none`, `--mine`, `--label <label>`, `--all`, `--limit 100`.
- `gh dojo next` and `gh dojo list` read the board a few seconds behind writes: an issue just created or moved may be missing or in its old status. To check one issue, `gh dojo show N`.

## Creating and linking issues

- `gh dojo new "<title>" --type <type> --body "…"`: the issue, its labels, the board in `Backlog`, in one command; a long body: `--body-file <file>`, or `--body-file -` for stdin. Also `--area <area>`, `--label <label>`, `--assignee @me`, `--milestone <title>`, `--blocked-by N`, `--parent N`, each checked before anything is created. `--type bug` adds the label `type: bug`; the types are the repository's labels starting with `type: `, and an unknown one fails listing them.
- `gh dojo comment N "text"`: a comment without changing the status.
- `gh dojo block N --by M` / `gh dojo unblock N --by M`: add or remove a blocked-by link without changing the status. An existing issue becomes a sub-issue with `gh issue edit N --parent M`.
- A commit pushed without a pull request names its issue after a keyword in its message, as `Refs #12`; parentheses at the end of the first line, `(#12)`, do not count here: that is how `gh dojo release` finds the issues a release includes.

## Errors and repeats

On an error, do what its `fix:` line says. Exit code 2 is a process check refusing: never work around it (do not move the status another way); ask the user. On 4 (network, rate limit or auth) and 5 (partially applied), run the same command again, on 4 a bit later. A repeat is safe: what is already in place (a status, the latest comment, a link) is skipped, and `new` with the same title finishes the issue it created.

# gh-dojo project notes

## Process: which verb when

- `ready` only when the change is **in main** (merged, tests green), not when it is done on a branch.
- `done` only when the change has shipped in a release; **never without the user's word**. For a release, read
  "Releases" in `CONTRIBUTING.md` first: this project's rules for `gh dojo release` and what to do with its output.
- A release is one command, not a sequence of your own: show the user `gh dojo release main --verb done --dry-run`
  and the notes, `script/release-notes.sh HEAD`, ask for the tag, and on their word run `make release TAG=vX.Y.Z` (`script/release.sh`: tag, push, wait for the
  release run, `gh extension install` of the release, move the release's issues to Done). It takes several minutes: run it in the background.
  After a failure, run it again with the same tag.
- `shipped` only for an issue opened for work that has already shipped (sub-issues split off after the fact):
  `gh dojo shipped N --comment "v0.4.1"`. Work done now goes through `start`, `ready` and `done`, and a
  release moves its issues with `--verb done`, never `--verb shipped`.
- In `--comment` for `ready` and `done` it helps to give the commit or release: `--comment "5fc0e30"`.
- A commit with a change users would notice adds `Changelog: <kind>: <text>` to its message, kind `breaking`,
  `added`, `changed` or `fixed`, text in the user's words: the release notes are made of these lines
  ("Release notes" in `CONTRIBUTING.md`). Internal commits have none.

## Inconvenience → a `dogfood` issue

Any inconvenience while working with gh-dojo (an unclear error, an extra step, a missing flag, help that lies, having
to work around it with `gh`): open an issue **right away**, without putting it off or quietly fixing it:

```sh
gh dojo new "<what is inconvenient, briefly>" --type dogfood --body "What I did: … What I expected: … What I got: …"
```

Then go on with the main task.

## Closing and reopening

Our config has no `drop` or `revive` verbs: to close an issue other than through `done` (not needed, a duplicate)
or to reopen one, use `gh issue close N --reason "not planned"` / `gh issue reopen N`, only on the user's decision.

## Which version runs

`gh dojo` is the latest release, installed with `gh extension install` (`gh dojo --version`): a change reaches it
only after the merge and a release.
